records.title: AvenaPay Disputes Analytics
records.summary: Disputes analytics that help merchants understand change, direct attention, and identify strong recovery opportunities.
records.content: AvenaPay Disputes management Turning dispute complexity into actionable clarity. A representative disputes analytics platform designed to help merchants manage high-volume chargebacks, understand what changed, identify what needs attention, and find the strongest recovery opportunities. The challenge Merchants struggled to understand which disputes were worth defending, why cases were being lost, and how to recover more funds without relying on manual reports from support or client services. Complex dispute data needed to become easier to understand, filter, and act on. My approach I designed the dashboard strategy, information architecture, dispute-health KPIs, probability scoring, filtered queue shortcuts, case detail views, alerts, custom reports, and natural-language analytics. The interface, branding, data, and identifying details were recreated to protect confidential work while preserving the product’s complexity and design strategy. 1 / 6 Lead with outcomesThe primary dashboard reframes disputes around recovery, loss, and performance—giving merchants an immediate understanding of what changed and where attention matters. Volume with meaningful contextTrends and comparisons help teams distinguish routine fluctuations from signals that require investigation, keeping raw case volume connected to business impact. Evidence where decisions happenThe case view brings status, value, evidence, timing, and recommended action into one workspace so merchants can move from analysis into resolution with confidence. Attention, carefully directedAlerts prioritize changes, deadlines, and high-value opportunities without turning every update into noise, helping teams intervene at the right moment. From operations to executive narrativeCustom reporting translates case activity into an outcome-oriented view leaders can use to understand performance, risk, and recovery over time. Natural-language analysisA conversational layer lets users investigate their dispute data in familiar language, shortening the path from an emerging question to a useful answer. records.title: LedgerFlow Payments and Invoicing
records.summary: A clearer fintech experience for invoices, payments, customers, reminders, reporting, and mobile collection.
records.content: LedgerFlow Payments and invoicing One understandable flow from invoice to payment. A modern fintech experience for businesses that need a clearer, calmer way to manage invoices, payments, customers, reminders, reporting, and mobile collection. The goal Getting paid should feel organized, trustworthy, and easy to act on—not scattered across disconnected tools or buried in confusing financial workflows. LedgerFlow needed to preserve the depth businesses rely on while making everyday financial work feel manageable. My approach I designed the core desktop and mobile flows, including the dashboard, reporting, invoice creation, payment links, customer billing, reminders, and payment collection. I focused on hierarchy, clarity, status visibility, and reusable patterns so users could quickly see what needed attention, what was handled, and where money was moving. 1 / 6 An actionable financial overviewThe dashboard prioritizes status, movement, and exceptions so users can understand what needs attention before entering a detailed workflow. Reporting connected to the workFinancial summaries remain close to the underlying activity, helping businesses understand performance without moving between disconnected reporting tools. Invoices organized by stateClear status, value, customer, and due-date signals let users distinguish what is moving normally from what needs a reminder or intervention. Create with confidenceThe invoice flow uses progressive structure and immediate context to make a detailed financial task feel guided without removing the control businesses need. Collections without the chaosPayment links, reminders, and collection activity share a common language, making the next action legible while preserving a complete record of what has happened. The same clarity on mobileThe mobile experience focuses the product around quick checks and high-value actions, extending the system without forcing a desktop interface into a smaller frame. records.title: LionFinancial Merchant Management System
records.summary: A connected operating system for merchant accounts, customers, transactions, approvals, payouts, reporting, and performance.
records.content: LionFinancial Merchant operations A calmer operating system for merchant performance. LionFinancial Merchant Management System brings the information behind a large merchant network into one connected experience, so teams can focus on decisions instead of wrangling disconnected tools. The challenge The people responsible for merchant performance are often forced to make important decisions from scattered systems, disconnected reports, and partial information. Simple questions become stressful: Which merchants are healthy? Which need attention? Where are transactions slowing down? What needs to be approved, scheduled, reported, or fixed? The design response I designed LMMS to connect accounts, customers, transactions, approvals, scheduled payouts, and reporting in a clearer operating environment. The experience streamlines the work around the data, helping teams understand performance and act without reconstructing the story across multiple platforms. 1 / 6 The merchant network as an operating viewA merchant list should do more than act as a directory. This view brings status, services, volume, recent activity, risk, approvals, onboarding, and network health together so platform teams can identify which businesses are growing and which need intervention without opening every record.Representative outcome 30% greater efficiency in merchant review by making risk, activity, adoption, and volume visible at the list level. Service configuration meets adoptionPayment methods affect cash flow, friction, and revenue opportunity. I paired configuration with adoption so teams can see what is enabled, how many merchants use it, the volume and fees it drives, and where setup requests are waiting—shifting the question from “Is it on?” to “Is it creating value?”Representative outcome A 15–20% improvement in the ease of driving service adoption, visibility, and conversion. Customer behavior as a merchant-health signalVolume alone does not explain business health. Active customers, repeat purchase rate, payment preferences, lifetime value, support issues, and health scores reveal whether a merchant is retaining customers or beginning to lose momentum—and give platform teams a stronger basis for advising them.Representative outcome A projected 35–60% improvement in merchant advisory conversations through clearer customer and payment-behavior signals. Predictable future money movementI reframed scheduled payments as a financial-operations tool supporting vendor payouts, platform fees, settlements, lease payments, payroll advances, insurance premiums, and merchant disbursements. Upcoming, successful, and failed activity remains visible alongside reusable templates because uncertainty is the enemy when users are responsible for money movement. Reporting without rebuilding the workA report library, scheduled reports, saved views, quick exports, ownership, dates, and categories turn historical reporting into reusable operational knowledge. Teams can generate leadership summaries, monitor merchants and payouts, export what they need, and move on without repeatedly reconstructing the same analysis.Representative outcome Approximately 80% less report-preparation time. From audit trail to pattern recognitionThe transaction table covers payments, refunds, disputes, payouts, settlement timing, fees, methods, and status across merchants. Supporting views expose mix, volume by time of day, and settlement aging so users can move from “What happened?” to “What does this mean?” without exporting the data first.Representative outcome A projected 50–75% reduction in manual transaction research and export dependency, depending on the business and user. records.title: Northstar Commerce Conversion Experience
records.summary: A conversion-focused experience for understanding offers, comparing payment products and rates, and choosing the right setup.
records.content: Northstar Commerce Conversion strategy A clearer path from first impression to confident conversion. A conversion-focused commerce experience that helps small business owners understand the offer, compare payment products and rates, and choose the right setup for how they sell. The opportunity The page needed to feel more approachable than a typical fintech experience while still communicating legitimacy, trust, and business value. Product choices and competitive rates had to become easier to evaluate without making the experience feel pushy or overbuilt. My approach I designed the landing-page structure, visual direction, product presentation, CTA strategy, trust-building sections, responsive direction, and supporting brand elements. Color, spacing, and progressive information reduce cognitive load while guiding visitors through a clear conversion path. 1 / 6 Make the offer immediately legibleThe opening establishes audience, value, and next action quickly, using approachable product presentation to make a fintech decision feel less intimidating. Translate features into business valueThe narrative moves from the product promise into recognizable small-business needs, helping visitors see how the platform fits the way they already sell. Make comparison feel manageableProduct options are structured around meaningful differences so visitors can evaluate fit without decoding a dense matrix or leaving the conversion path. Use transparency to build trustPricing and rates are introduced with enough context to support evaluation, balancing clarity with the nuance required for different business models. Reduce risk before asking for commitmentSupport, proof, and trust signals answer the doubts that naturally appear late in consideration, strengthening confidence without relying on aggressive persuasion. End with a clear next stepThe final invitation resolves the story into a focused action, preserving the page’s friendly tone while making the path forward unmistakable. records.title: Paladin Wireframing Kit
records.summary: An accessibility-minded wireframing system for exploring structure, workflows, content priorities, and edge cases.
records.content: Paladin UX framing kit A shared language for solving complex product problems. A reusable wireframing system that helps teams explore structure, workflow, content priorities, accessibility, and edge cases before visual polish gets in the way. Why it was needed Early product work gets messy when teams jump into high-fidelity design before understanding user needs, information hierarchy, workflow logic, interaction states, and edge cases. Paladin was designed to let that confusion melt away and bring the UX problem into focus. The system I created reusable, accessibility-minded components, established patterns, and annotation-friendly layouts for complex tables, reporting, payment workflows, and data-heavy products. The kit helps teams align earlier, uncover challenges sooner, reduce rework, and move more confidently into detailed design. 1 / 6 Structure before stylingDashboard and visualization frames help teams establish hierarchy, comparison, and decision priority before color or brand details influence the conversation. Dense data with a clear jobTable patterns account for scanning, filtering, bulk actions, pagination, status, and empty states so teams can solve the workflow around the data—not merely draw rows. Make consequential flows discussablePayment and workflow frames expose steps, validation, decision points, and recovery states early, when changing the experience is still inexpensive. Reporting as a reusable patternFlexible reporting structures help teams test what should be summarized, compared, saved, scheduled, and exported before committing to a final interface. Small controls, explicit behaviorFoundational controls include interaction and state considerations so accessibility and behavioral consistency enter the discussion alongside layout. Breadth without prescriptionCommerce patterns demonstrate how the kit adapts to distinct product domains while remaining neutral enough for teams to explore their own content and business rules. records.title: Product Design Leadership Principles
records.summary: The throughline
records.content: The throughline Every challenge is different. Progress starts with clarity. Across platforms, systems, and teams, my role is consistent: make complexity understandable, create the structure people need to move together, and turn ambitious product decisions into work that can scale. Clarity before complexity Start with the decisions people need to make, then shape the product around helping them make those decisions well. Systems that create momentum Build reusable foundations that improve quality and speed without flattening the needs of the product or the people using it. Leadership through execution Align teams around a direction, stay close enough to the work to protect its intent, and help strong ideas make it into the product. What comes next If your team is entering unfamiliar product territory, let’s create a clear path forward together. See more in Figma Start a conversation

records.title: Vega Product Design System
records.summary: A shared foundation of components, tokens, documentation, and practices for global product teams.
records.content: Global Payments Enterprise design system A north star for product design across a global ecosystem. All roads intersect at Vega—a shared foundation for software product design across three continents, numerous countries, and distributed product, design, and engineering teams. Visit Vega The opportunity Our product ecosystem needed a stronger shared foundation—one that could make products more consistent, accessible, and thoughtfully designed without slowing teams down or preventing them from solving for their own product needs. My leadership As design system lead and product design manager, I kicked off and led Vega’s creation and evolution across reusable components, accessibility standards, design tokens, documentation, governance, and Figma-to-code alignment. I partnered closely with engineering to reduce rework and help teams build better software with greater speed and confidence. 1 / 6 A foundation teams can shareVega establishes common visual and interaction foundations so separate products can feel like parts of one ecosystem without erasing their individual requirements. Components with intentReusable components pair visual consistency with behavioral guidance, helping designers and engineers understand not only what to use, but why and when to use it. Patterns for real product workThe system moves beyond isolated UI pieces into repeatable product patterns, giving teams a faster path through common workflows and complex states. Accessibility built into the decisionStandards and usage guidance bring accessibility into component selection and interaction design from the beginning instead of treating it as a final audit. A durable bridge to codeShared tokens and aligned naming reduce translation between Figma and engineering, protecting decisions as components move from design into production. Documentation that supports adoptionClear examples, governance, and contribution guidance make the system usable across distributed teams and give it a structure that can evolve with the organization. I paired configuration with adoption so teams can see what is enabled, how many merchants use it, the volume and fees it drives, and where setup requests are waiting—shifting the question from “Is it on?” to “Is it creating value?”Representative outcome A 15–20% improvement in the ease of driving service adoption, visibility, and conversion. Customer behavior as a merchant-health signalVolume alone does not explain business health. Active customers, repeat purchase rate, payment preferences, lifetime value, support issues, and health scores reveal whether a merchant is retaining customers or beginning to lose momentum—and give platform teams a stronger basis for advising them.Representative outcome A projected 35–60% improvement in merchant advisory conversations through clearer customer and payment-behavior signals. Predictable future money movementI reframed scheduled payments as a financial-operations tool supporting vendor payouts, platform fees, settlements, lease payments, payroll advances, insurance premiums, and merchant disbursements. Upcoming, successful, and failed activity remains visible alongside reusable templates because uncertainty is the enemy when users are responsible for money movement. Reporting without rebuilding the workA report library, scheduled reports, saved views, quick exports, ownership, dates, and categories turn historical reporting into reusable operational knowledge. Teams can generate leadership summaries, monitor merchants and payouts, export what they need, and move on without repeatedly reconstructing the same analysis.Representative outcome Approximately 80% less report-preparation time. From audit trail to pattern recognitionThe transaction table covers payments, refunds, disputes, payouts, settlement timing, fees, methods, and status across merchants. Supporting views expose mix, volume by time of day, and settlement aging so users can move from “What happened?” to “What does this mean?” without exporting the data first.Representative outcome A projected 50–75% reduction in manual transaction research and export dependency, depending on the business and user. Global Payments Enterprise design system A north star for product design across a global ecosystem. All roads intersect at Vega—a shared foundation for software product design across three continents, numerous countries, and distributed product, design, and engineering teams. Visit Vega The opportunity Our product ecosystem needed a stronger shared foundation—one that could make products more consistent, accessible, and thoughtfully designed without slowing teams down or preventing them from solving for their own product needs. My leadership As design system lead and product design manager, I kicked off and led Vega’s creation and evolution across reusable components, accessibility standards, design tokens, documentation, governance, and Figma-to-code alignment. I partnered closely with engineering to reduce rework and help teams build better software with greater speed and confidence. 1 / 6 A foundation teams can shareVega establishes common visual and interaction foundations so separate products can feel like parts of one ecosystem without erasing their individual requirements. Components with intentReusable components pair visual consistency with behavioral guidance, helping designers and engineers understand not only what to use, but why and when to use it. Patterns for real product workThe system moves beyond isolated UI pieces into repeatable product patterns, giving teams a faster path through common workflows and complex states. Accessibility built into the decisionStandards and usage guidance bring accessibility into component selection and interaction design from the beginning instead of treating it as a final audit. A durable bridge to codeShared tokens and aligned naming reduce translation between Figma and engineering, protecting decisions as components move from design into production. Documentation that supports adoptionClear examples, governance, and contribution guidance make the system usable across distributed teams and give it a structure that can evolve with the organization. AvenaPay Disputes management Turning dispute complexity into actionable clarity. A representative disputes analytics platform designed to help merchants manage high-volume chargebacks, understand what changed, identify what needs attention, and find the strongest recovery opportunities. The challenge Merchants struggled to understand which disputes were worth defending, why cases were being lost, and how to recover more funds without relying on manual reports from support or client services. Complex dispute data needed to become easier to understand, filter, and act on. My approach I designed the dashboard strategy, information architecture, dispute-health KPIs, probability scoring, filtered queue shortcuts, case detail views, alerts, custom reports, and natural-language analytics. The interface, branding, data, and identifying details were recreated to protect confidential work while preserving the product’s complexity and design strategy. 1 / 6 Lead with outcomesThe primary dashboard reframes disputes around recovery, loss, and performance—giving merchants an immediate understanding of what changed and where attention matters. Volume with meaningful contextTrends and comparisons help teams distinguish routine fluctuations from signals that require investigation, keeping raw case volume connected to business impact. Evidence where decisions happenThe case view brings status, value, evidence, timing, and recommended action into one workspace so merchants can move from analysis into resolution with confidence. Attention, carefully directedAlerts prioritize changes, deadlines, and high-value opportunities without turning every update into noise, helping teams intervene at the right moment. From operations to executive narrativeCustom reporting translates case activity into an outcome-oriented view leaders can use to understand performance, risk, and recovery over time. Natural-language analysisA conversational layer lets users investigate their dispute data in familiar language, shortening the path from an emerging question to a useful answer. Paladin UX framing kit A shared language for solving complex product problems. A reusable wireframing system that helps teams explore structure, workflow, content priorities, accessibility, and edge cases before visual polish gets in the way. Why it was needed Early product work gets messy when teams jump into high-fidelity design before understanding user needs, information hierarchy, workflow logic, interaction states, and edge cases. Paladin was designed to let that confusion melt away and bring the UX problem into focus. The system I created reusable, accessibility-minded components, established patterns, and annotation-friendly layouts for complex tables, reporting, payment workflows, and data-heavy products. The kit helps teams align earlier, uncover challenges sooner, reduce rework, and move more confidently into detailed design. 1 / 6 Structure before stylingDashboard and visualization frames help teams establish hierarchy, comparison, and decision priority before color or brand details influence the conversation. Dense data with a clear jobTable patterns account for scanning, filtering, bulk actions, pagination, status, and empty states so teams can solve the workflow around the data—not merely draw rows. Make consequential flows discussablePayment and workflow frames expose steps, validation, decision points, and recovery states early, when changing the experience is still inexpensive. Reporting as a reusable patternFlexible reporting structures help teams test what should be summarized, compared, saved, scheduled, and exported before committing to a final interface. Small controls, explicit behaviorFoundational controls include interaction and state considerations so accessibility and behavioral consistency enter the discussion alongside layout. Breadth without prescriptionCommerce patterns demonstrate how the kit adapts to distinct product domains while remaining neutral enough for teams to explore their own content and business rules. LedgerFlow Payments and invoicing One understandable flow from invoice to payment. A modern fintech experience for businesses that need a clearer, calmer way to manage invoices, payments, customers, reminders, reporting, and mobile collection. The goal Getting paid should feel organized, trustworthy, and easy to act on—not scattered across disconnected tools or buried in confusing financial workflows. LedgerFlow needed to preserve the depth businesses rely on while making everyday financial work feel manageable. My approach I designed the core desktop and mobile flows, including the dashboard, reporting, invoice creation, payment links, customer billing, reminders, and payment collection. I focused on hierarchy, clarity, status visibility, and reusable patterns so users could quickly see what needed attention, what was handled, and where money was moving. 1 / 6 An actionable financial overviewThe dashboard prioritizes status, movement, and exceptions so users can understand what needs attention before entering a detailed workflow. Reporting connected to the workFinancial summaries remain close to the underlying activity, helping businesses understand performance without moving between disconnected reporting tools. Invoices organized by stateClear status, value, customer, and due-date signals let users distinguish what is moving normally from what needs a reminder or intervention. Create with confidenceThe invoice flow uses progressive structure and immediate context to make a detailed financial task feel guided without removing the control businesses need. Collections without the chaosPayment links, reminders, and collection activity share a common language, making the next action legible while preserving a complete record of what has happened. The same clarity on mobileThe mobile experience focuses the product around quick checks and high-value actions, extending the system without forcing a desktop interface into a smaller frame. Northstar Commerce Conversion strategy A clearer path from first impression to confident conversion. A conversion-focused commerce experience that helps small business owners understand the offer, compare payment products and rates, and choose the right setup for how they sell. The opportunity The page needed to feel more approachable than a typical fintech experience while still communicating legitimacy, trust, and business value. Product choices and competitive rates had to become easier to evaluate without making the experience feel pushy or overbuilt. My approach I designed the landing-page structure, visual direction, product presentation, CTA strategy, trust-building sections, responsive direction, and supporting brand elements. Color, spacing, and progressive information reduce cognitive load while guiding visitors through a clear conversion path. 1 / 6 Make the offer immediately legibleThe opening establishes audience, value, and next action quickly, using approachable product presentation to make a fintech decision feel less intimidating. Translate features into business valueThe narrative moves from the product promise into recognizable small-business needs, helping visitors see how the platform fits the way they already sell. Make comparison feel manageableProduct options are structured around meaningful differences so visitors can evaluate fit without decoding a dense matrix or leaving the conversion path. Use transparency to build trustPricing and rates are introduced with enough context to support evaluation, balancing clarity with the nuance required for different business models. Reduce risk before asking for commitmentSupport, proof, and trust signals answer the doubts that naturally appear late in consideration, strengthening confidence without relying on aggressive persuasion. End with a clear next stepThe final invitation resolves the story into a focused action, preserving the page’s friendly tone while making the path forward unmistakable. The throughline Every challenge is different. Progress starts with clarity. Across platforms, systems, and teams, my role is consistent: make complexity understandable, create the structure people need to move together, and turn ambitious product decisions into work that can scale. Clarity before complexity Start with the decisions people need to make, then shape the product around helping them make those decisions well. Systems that create momentum Build reusable foundations that improve quality and speed without flattening the needs of the product or the people using it. Leadership through execution Align teams around a direction, stay close enough to the work to protect its intent, and help strong ideas make it into the product. What comes next If your team is entering unfamiliar product territory, let’s create a clear path forward together. records.summary: Terms of use and privacy information for janmichael.io, including analytics, local browser storage, external services, and contact details.
records.content: Terms of Use and Privacy Policy Effective Date These Terms of Use and this Privacy Policy are effective as of July 15, 2026. Purpose of This Site This website is a personal portfolio for Jan Michael Wallace II. It shares professional information, selected work, perspectives, and ways to get in touch about projects, collaborations, or professional conversations. Information Used by This Site This site uses a small amount of browser-based functionality to make the experience work as intended. When you submit the contact form, your first name, last name, email address, subject, message, and related request information are transmitted to Web3Forms. Web3Forms processes the submission and forwards it to my email inbox. The email address you provide is used as the reply-to address for that message. If you respond to the consent banner, your analytics choice is stored locally in your browser as janmichaelConsentPreference. This prevents the site from asking for the same choice on every visit. This site also uses JavaScript to adjust the header while scrolling and to load recent article content for the Perspectives page. Those features are used to display the site and its content properly. Analytics and Third-Party Services This site can load Google Tag Manager and related Google services to understand general site activity and improve the website. Google Tag Manager is only loaded after you accept analytics in the consent banner. Web3Forms provides the contact-form processing service. It may retain form submissions and related technical data and use infrastructure or spam-prevention providers as described in the Web3Forms Privacy Policy. Third-party services may process technical information such as browser details, device information, IP address, referring pages, pages visited, or interaction events according to their own policies. This site does not control those third-party services. The Perspectives page may request article feed data through third-party feed or proxy services so recent writing can be displayed. How Information Is Used I use information received through this site only for its intended purpose: operating the website, displaying content, improving the site experience, and responding to messages you choose to send. I will not sell your personal information. I will not use inquiry information for unrelated marketing, profiling, or any purpose unrelated to responding to your inquiry or maintaining this website. Your Choices You can choose not to submit the contact form and can email me directly instead. You can also clear this site's local browser storage through your browser settings if you want to remove your saved analytics preference. You may use browser settings, privacy tools, or extensions to limit cookies, local storage, JavaScript, analytics, or third-party requests. Blocking Web3Forms or other required services may prevent the contact form from submitting. Content and Intellectual Property Unless otherwise noted, the writing, design, code, images, logos, and other materials on this site belong to Jan Michael Wallace II or are used with permission. You may view and share links to this site, but you may not copy, republish, or reuse site content in a way that suggests ownership, endorsement, or affiliation without permission. External Links This site links to external websites and services, including social platforms, portfolio platforms, article platforms, and email providers. Those websites are governed by their own terms and privacy practices. No Warranty This site is provided as-is for general informational and portfolio purposes. I try to keep the content accurate and available, but I do not guarantee that the site will always be error-free, uninterrupted, or current. Changes to These Terms and Policy These terms and this privacy policy may be updated from time to time as the site changes. The effective date above will be updated when material changes are made. Contact Questions about these terms, this privacy policy, or this site's use of information can be sent to hello@janmichael.io.

records.content: Jan is a product design leader specializing in UX strategy, accessibility, enterprise product design, and design systems. With experience leading complex fintech and SaaS initiatives, he transforms fragmented workflows into scalable, intuitive experiences that improve usability and business outcomes. Combining design leadership with front-end development expertise, Jan bridges product, engineering, and business teams to deliver polished, user-centered solutions.
